hypothesis: The radio platform binding composes the real shared PMIC provider, rail ledger, clock registry, pin manager, SDIO controller and card worker with the required power and reset sequencing.
conclusion: The composition passed on the host model; physical radio operation is unqualified.
narrative: checks/a733-radio-platform.py (removed from the repository as a one-off composition superseded by the radio-network check) composed the real shared PMIC provider, rail ledger, clock registry, pin manager, SDIO controller and card worker against modeled registers under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, which reported no errors. It verified: actual resource acquisition, copied PMIC results and request reap; ten milliseconds between PM1-low admission and enable, fifty milliseconds before module clocks and card access, and ten microseconds before reset release; SDC1 preparation and card enumeration with exclusive controller/module scopes; one downstream borrower, PM0 input, forged-token and aliased-output refusal; fresh deadlines after consumed completion and retention after active expiry; wrong observed supply voltage before pin or controller changes; retained common-mutex ownership after an uncertain clock write. The platform core compiled for native AArch64 and its adapter against the actual single-core and SMP FreeRTOS configurations. Existing PMIC, SDIO transfer, firmware upload and radio protocol checks were reused without repetition. The input manifest preserved 101 source, dependency and compiler identities; saved commands, log and native objects record the batch. No physical board execution or performance measurement was performed. The design directory holds the source identities and inspected board design: A733 User Manual V1.00 sections 4.1 and 11.3, pin-function tables, board schematic V1.2 sheets 6, 9 and 14, and the pinned board device tree.
